biography.plain_text: Jack MacKeddie is an Australian maritime businessman associated with the Queenscliff–Sorrento ferry service across Port Phillip. He rose from skipper to general manager of Peninsula Searoad Transport and became its managing director. With merchant banker John Barnes and Cummins, he also bought Southern Marine Shiplift, a shipyard in Launceston, Tasmania.

long_biography.plain_text:
Ferry operator Jack MacKeddie helped repair a damaged Peninsula Searoad vessel by taking it to an engineering works in Western Port. He and a colleague removed its bent driveshaft in the mud, and the engineering company straightened it. The ferry returned to service within two days.

An earlier hovercraft venture had proved more costly. MacKeddie launched a commuter service linking the Mornington Peninsula with Melbourne, then switched to tourist trips when demand disappointed. A fire ended the venture. The experience sharpened his attention to the fuel and maintenance costs of fast passenger transport.
